stories.title: A Pretty Sweet Victory
stories.summary: Sonntag and her team, specializing in baked goods, expanded their skills using unfamiliar ingredients like jicama to compete on 'Foodtastic,' ultimately returning to Michigan as champions. Sonntag plans to grow her business, moving to a larger space and hiring more staff, while reflecting on her 20-year career and mentors. The team's episodes air on Disney+.

photo.alt: A Pretty Sweet Victory

stories.title: Amway and affiliates agree to pay $225 million to settle lawsuit over alleged deception of workers
stories.summary: Amway, headquartered near Grand Rapids, Michigan, and two affiliates have agreed to a $225 million settlement with the FTC to resolve claims of deceiving workers about potential earnings. The FTC alleges that Amway misled Independent Business Owners (IBOs) with false income claims, while the company disputes the allegations. The settlement requires changes to business practices, including a requirement for IBOs to sell 70% of purchased products monthly.

photo.alt: Amway's world headquarters is in Ada, Michigan, about 10 miles from Grand Rapids.

stories.title: Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum Closed for Scheduled Maintenance Sept 14-18
stories.summary: The Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum will be closed from September 14 to 18 for scheduled maintenance, with normal operations resuming on September 19. The institution's mission focuses on inspiring curiosity and exploration in STEM and the natural world through discovery-based learning.

photo.alt: Ann Arbor Hands-On Museum Closed for Scheduled Maintenance Sept 14-18

stories.title: CANCELED – Sol Beats Beach Fiesta presented by Diversified Members Credit Union
stories.summary: The Sol Beats Beach Fiesta at Campus Martius Park, scheduled for September 19, 2026, has been canceled due to forecasted inclement weather. The event was to feature DJ Sabor and giveaways as part of the Beach Parties series.

photo.alt: CANCELED – Sol Beats Beach Fiesta presented by Diversified Members Credit Union

stories.title: CANCELLED: Bubble Fest: Broadway Park West
stories.summary: The Bubble Fest at Broadway Park West has been cancelled due to weather and will be rescheduled for a date TBA. The event was to feature bubble machines, bubble blowing, kids' activities, and surprises from the Detroit Circus, along with pizza and ice cream sales.

photo.alt: Ann Arbor Observer header image

stories.title: Department of Public Safety hosts bike registration events for students
stories.summary: Eastern Michigan University's Department of Public Safety is hosting free bike and scooter registration events on Sept. 15 and Sept. 21 to allow students to legally use their vehicles on campus. Registration requires completing a form with personal and vehicle details, and registered bikes will receive identification stickers to aid in recovery if stolen. The first three registrants at each event will receive a free U-lock.

photo.alt: Department of Public Safety hosts bike registration events for students

stories.title: Detroit family says woman was mistakenly cremated before funeral viewing
stories.summary: The family of Kimberlly Moore, who died from endometrial cancer, claims her body was mistakenly cremated before her scheduled viewing at Hutchison Funeral Home. They discovered another woman’s body during the viewing and are demanding answers, while the funeral home’s PR representative said an internal investigation would be conducted.

photo.alt: Detroit family says woman was mistakenly cremated before funeral viewing

stories.title: Detroit Red Wings management changes and team instability
stories.summary: The Detroit Red Wings are in disarray after Steve Yzerman stepped down as GM and the team announced Shawn Horcoff as interim GM. Recent moves like removing Dylan Larkin's captaincy and vague injury reports suggest poor management decisions.

photo.alt: Al Goldis / AP

stories.title: Detroit Tenants Union Lawsuit: Evictions and Compliance
stories.summary: The Detroit Tenants Union lawsuit challenges eviction practices tied to housing compliance, with landlords warning of market collapse due to maintenance costs and tenants arguing safety shouldn't depend on profitability. The next hearing is set for Sept. 21, where a judge may rule on a motion to dismiss the case.

photo.alt: A row of older red-brick-and-wood houses with porches and trees line the street under a gray, overcast sky.

stories.title: Downriver Recovery Festival brings music, art, and support together
stories.summary: The first Recovery & Resilience Festival in Detroit's Hamtramck neighborhood on Sept. 20 will feature guest speaker Lol Tolhurst of The Cure. The event, organized by the Downriver Council for the Arts and Passenger Recovery, combines music, art, and recovery support through creative programming and community engagement.

photo.alt: Passenger Recovery provides support, resources and creative programming for people in recovery.

stories.title: Driver killed in fiery Grand Rapids crash
stories.summary: A driver died Sunday morning, Sept. 20, in a fiery crash near Century Avenue SW and McKendrick Street SW in Grand Rapids. The vehicle collided with a tree and caught fire, with the driver pronounced dead at the scene. Police are investigating the incident.

photo.alt: Grand Rapids police investigating fatal crash on southwest side.

stories.title: Early spark fades as Eastern Michigan Football drops road contest at Wisconsin, 54-10
stories.summary: Eastern Michigan University's football team initially led but fell 54-10 to Wisconsin in a road game on Sept. 19, 2026. Despite an early defensive takeaway and strong opening drive, Wisconsin's explosive second-quarter surge proved decisive. The Badgers' quarterback Colton Joseph recorded 362 passing yards, while Eastern Michigan's Noah Kim totaled 140 passing yards.

photo.alt: Early spark fades as Eastern Michigan Football drops road contest at Wisconsin, 54-10

stories.title: EMU President Dr. Brendan Kelly uses investiture to focus on student achievement and well-being
stories.summary: A large crowd of students, faculty, staff, and alumni attended the investiture of Dr. Brendan Kelly as Eastern Michigan’s 24th President. During his address, Kelly emphasized the importance of focusing on student success and community engagement in higher education, stating that universities must ensure students are visible and supported as individuals in a digital world.

photo.alt: Dr. Brendan Kelly addresses the crowd at his investiture on September 18, 2026.

stories.title: EMU to officially induct Brendan Kelly as president
stories.summary: Eastern Michigan University will hold the presidential investiture of Brendan Kelly on Sept. 18, 2026, at 2 p.m. in Pease Auditorium. Kelly, who began serving as president on April 1, 2026, will be inducted as the 24th president by the EMU Board of Regents. The public ceremony includes a post-event reception in Sill Hall.

photo.alt: EMU to officially induct Brendan Kelly as president

stories.title: Federal judge dismisses lawsuit over Title X grant funding for pregnancy prevention efforts
stories.summary: A federal judge dismissed a lawsuit challenging Title X grant funding for pregnancy prevention efforts, upholding the allocation of these federal health care funds for related programs in Michigan.

photo.alt: Michigan Advance logo

stories.title: Festival of Oddities to move. Organizer says Charlotte is unwelcoming
stories.summary: The organizer of the Festival of Oddities has announced the event will no longer take place in Charlotte due to harassment by a local religious group and inadequate support from city officials. Jenn Carpenter, a festival founder, cited safety concerns and a lack of police response during protests by a church group. The festival, held annually since 2019, plans to relocate to another Mid-Michigan community in 2027.

photo.alt: Portrait of Dan Basso

stories.title: Former Metro Detroit doctor sentenced to 9 years in multi-state child porn case
stories.summary: A former Metro Detroit doctor, Lincoln Erickson, was sentenced to nine years in prison for a federal child pornography charge. The multi-state investigation led to the arrest of four men, including Erickson, who shared explicit materials and discussed sexually abusing children. Erickson, 32, of Farmington Hills, was found with videos of minors and AI-generated child pornography on his phone.

source.name: Jenny Sherman, Dane Kelly, Erika Erickson

photo.alt: Lincoln Erickson (WDIV)

stories.title: Former Michigan House speaker slated for Sept. 21 trial amid accusations of misusing political funds
stories.summary: Former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield is set for a Sept. 21 trial on 13 felony charges, including criminal enterprise and embezzlement, related to misuse of funds from his political action committees and the Peninsula Fund. His wife Stephanie was recently sentenced for embezzling from the same fund, while the attorney general's office closed a prior sexual assault investigation due to insufficient evidence. The case involves testimony from former aides and allegations of improper mileage reimbursements and personal use of social welfare organization funds.

photo.alt: By Anna Liz Nichols/Michigan Advance

stories.title: Former Michigan WR scores two TDs in UCLA’s Big Ten win
stories.summary: Former Michigan wide receiver Semaj Morgan recorded two touchdowns in UCLA's 52-38 win over Purdue. Both scores came in the first quarter, with a 20-yard reception and a 27-yard catch-and-run. Morgan now leads UCLA with 12 receptions and 158 yards through three games.

photo.alt: Former Michigan wide receiver Semaj Morgan

stories.title: Freeland man charged with sexualizing, exploiting girl allegedly told detectives her mom ‘encouraged relationship’
stories.summary: Already charged on the state level with producing sexualized imagery of minor girls, a Freeland man is now facing related charges in the federal realm. Nikolas J. Clark, 22, on Sept. 15 appeared before U.S. District Magistrate Judge Patricia T. Morris, who informed him he had been charged with sexual exploitation of a minor, attempted coercion and enticement of a minor, and receipt of and/or distribution of child sexually abusive material.

photo.alt: Freeland man charged with sexualizing, exploiting girl allegedly told detectives her mom ‘encouraged relationship’

stories.title: Freeway shooting on I-94 in metro Detroit under investigation
stories.summary: Michigan State Police are investigating a shooting on eastbound I-94 in Roseville that left one person injured. The incident occurred around 11:30 p.m. Saturday, Sept. 19, with the injured individual taken to a hospital. A portion of the freeway was temporarily closed during the investigation.

photo.alt: Michigan State Police

stories.title: Funeral home launches internal review after woman was mistakenly cremated
stories.summary: Hutchison Funeral Home has launched an internal review after the family of Kimberlly Moore, who died from endometrial cancer, discovered her body was mistakenly cremated before a scheduled viewing. The family noticed the error when an employee unzipped a body bag that lacked a mole on Moore's toe, and they have received conflicting information about the availability of her ashes.

photo.alt: Funeral home error

stories.title: GVSU football sets program scoring record in 96-0 win over Judson
stories.summary: Grand Valley State set a program scoring record with a 96-0 victory over Judson, breaking their previous mark of 91 points. The Lakers fell short of the Division II record but coach Scott Wooster chose not to reach 100 points out of respect for the opponent. The game featured 10 touchdown drives, three quarterbacks combining for 18/18 passing, and special teams scoring two punt returns for touchdowns.

photo.alt: Grand Valley State players huddle before a game from a previous season

stories.title: High stakes embezzlement case against former GOP Michigan House speaker goes to trial next week
stories.summary: The trial of former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield for alleged financial crimes is set to begin on Sept. 22, 2026. Chatfield faces 13 felony charges, including embezzlement from a nonprofit organization, and has pleaded not guilty. His wife and associates previously pleaded guilty to related charges and may testify against him during the trial.

photo.alt: High stakes embezzlement case against former GOP Michigan House speaker goes to trial next week

stories.title: High stakes embezzlement case against former GOP Michigan House speaker goes to trial next week
stories.summary: Former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield faces trial on Sept. 22 for 13 felony charges including embezzlement from a nonprofit. He has pleaded not guilty, with his attorney claiming the case is politically motivated. The trial involves allegations of using funds from the Peninsula Fund for personal expenses and a kickback scheme, with his wife and associates already pleading guilty to related charges.

photo.alt: High stakes embezzlement case against former GOP Michigan House speaker goes to trial next week

stories.title: How the Gordie Howe Bridge is putting a historic Detroit landmark back on the map
stories.summary: One of Detroit’s most historic — and overlooked — landmarks is seeing more traffic than it has in decades, all thanks to the new Gordie Howe International Bridge, which has been open for about seven weeks. Historic Fort Wayne, the sprawling military and Indigenous site along the Detroit River, is seeing more foot traffic than it has in decades. Visitors drawn to the bridge’s new pedestrian path are stopping, exploring, and asking questions—and the city is paying attention.

photo.alt: How the Gordie Howe Bridge is putting a historic Detroit landmark back on the map

stories.title: How to preapply for home repair help in Detroit
stories.summary: Detroit residents can preapply for home repair assistance through the Critical Home Repair and LeadSafe Housing programs until Sept. 22, 2026. The city plans to repair about 350 homes annually, prioritizing urgent issues like plumbing, accessibility, and lead hazards. Thousands have applied in the past, but funding limitations mean long waitlists remain.

photo.alt: Abandoned house in Detroit

stories.title: How to preapply for home repair help in Detroit
stories.summary: Check if you’re eligible, then add your name to the list through Sept. 22.

photo.alt: How to preapply for home repair help in Detroit

stories.title: Huntington’s disease families find hope, community at Michigan HDSA Team Hope Walk
stories.summary: Families affected by Huntington’s disease gathered in Royal Oak for the Michigan Chapter of the Huntington’s Disease Society of America’s Team Hope Walk, an event designed to raise awareness, build community, and fund research for a disease with no cure.

photo.alt: Participants at Huntington's Disease Team Hope Walk in Royal Oak

stories.title: Income tax brackets changing in 2027: What you can expect
stories.summary: Federal tax brackets are expected to inch up next year, according to the latest estimates. The change means people will be allowed to earn more before their income is taxed at a higher rate.

photo.alt: Income tax brackets changing in 2027: What you can expect

stories.title: Investigation into shooting on I-94 in Macomb County on Saturday night
stories.summary: One person was taken to the hospital after a reported shooting along I-94 in Macomb County near Roseville on Saturday night. The incident occurred around 11:30 PM in the Eastbound lanes near 12 Mile Road, leading to a temporary closure of the interstate. Authorities are seeking witnesses to aid in the investigation.

photo.alt: Police investigation on I-94 after shooting

stories.title: Joe Pug & Willie Watson
stories.summary: Joe Pug, known for his lyrical acumen and harmonica style, transitioned from carpentry to Chicago's music scene. Willie Watson's formative encounter with Ruby Love in 1997 led to his folk music journey and eventual co-founding of Old Crow Medicine Show.

stories.title: Lillian Li Discusses Her Novel 'Bad Asians'
stories.summary: Author Lillian Li discusses her novel 'Bad Asians,' which explores the lives of high-achieving individuals coming of age during the Great Recession.

photo.alt: Stateside podcast cover image

stories.title: Madison Heights woman accused of trafficking victim brought her child along, prosecutors say
stories.summary: A Madison Heights woman faces human trafficking charges after a months-long investigation. Maya Scott Perry was arrested on June 17 for allegedly trafficking a woman for prostitution and bringing her minor child during activities, though the child was not harmed. She was arraigned on five felony charges and a misdemeanor, with a $250,000 bond, and is scheduled for a court appearance on September 18.

photo.alt: Maya Scott Perry (Courtesy of Madison Heights Police Department)

stories.title: Marching bands: See the winners from the Jenison Invitational
stories.summary: Rockford High School captured the highest competitive score at the Jenison Invitational marching band competition Saturday, Sept. 19, finishing with 79.250 points to win Flight I at Jenison High School.

photo.alt: Marching bands: See the winners from the Jenison Invitational

stories.title: Marching bands: See the winners from the Jenison Invitational
stories.summary: Rockford High School won the Jenison Invitational marching band competition on Sept. 19, 2026, with the highest score of 79.25 in Flight I, sweeping all three caption awards. The event, hosted at Jenison High School in Georgetown Twp., MI, featured multiple flights with bands from various schools competing in music, visual, and general effect categories.

photo.alt: Northview High School marching band performing at Jenison Invitational

stories.title: Meet the candidates running for US House of Representatives Michigan District 6
stories.summary: This article introduces the candidates running for the US House of Representatives in Michigan's 6th Congressional District, which includes all of Washtenaw County, most of Wayne County, and parts of Monroe and Oakland counties.

photo.alt: Candidates for Michigan's 6th Congressional District

stories.title: Mexican American Council’s ARPA funding compliance addressed by city leaders
stories.summary: Saginaw City Manager Tim Morales said an organization that received $620,000 in city-provided federal funds remains under compliance despite questions about the group’s eligibility. The Saginaw City Council approved multiple rounds of federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding for the Mexican American Council, including $500,000 in January 2023 and an additional $120,000 the following year. At the council’s Monday, Sept. 14 meeting, council members asked Morales for an update on the Mexican American Council’s status as an eligible recipient of the money. Media reports last week questioned the organization’s eligibility to receive ARPA funds as well as its status as a nonprofit.

photo.alt: Mexican American Council’s ARPA funding compliance addressed by city leaders

stories.title: Michigan AG candidate Doug Lloyd cut charges, sought no jail in sex-crime cases
stories.summary: Republican Doug Lloyd is running for Michigan attorney general on his three decades of experience as a prosecutor. However, a Metro Times review of court records and case files found instances during his tenure as Eaton County prosecutor where cases involving sexual assault, child exploitation, and domestic violence resulted in reduced charges, probation instead of jail, or no prosecution. The findings emerge as Lloyd faces Democrat Eli Savit in a closely contested race to succeed term-limited Attorney General Dana Nessel.

photo.alt: Doug Lloyd, Michigan AG candidate

stories.title: Michigan Court of Appeals directed to review convicted school shooter Ethan Crumbley's appeal of life without parole sentence
stories.summary: A Michigan court has directed a review of Ethan Crumbley's life without parole sentence for the 2021 Oxford High School shooting. The case involves determining if the teen should be eligible for parole after serving his sentence.

photo.alt: Oakland County Prosecutor Karen McDonald proceeds with an opening statement as defendant Ethan Crumbley listens in Pontiac, Michigan.

stories.title: Michigan launches project with crop insurance companies to reward regenerative farming
stories.summary: Michigan is launching a pilot project with crop insurance companies to recognize lower crop loss risk from regenerative farming practices. About 80 farmers in the Thumb region will participate, using AI analysis and soil samples to qualify for reduced insurance rates. The program aims to inform future national agricultural policies like the U.S. Farm Bill.

photo.alt: Early spring view of a Michigan farm.

stories.title: Michigan legacy Tommy Carr earns praise after memorable debut
stories.summary: Tommy Carr, a freshman quarterback with deep Michigan ties, made his college debut in the fourth quarter of Michigan's 52-17 win over UTEP, completing both pass attempts for 23 yards including a 19-yard touchdown. Head coach Kyle Whittingham praised Carr's performance, highlighting his speed, accuracy, and football IQ. Carr's family legacy includes his father, Jason Carr, and grandfather Lloyd Carr, former Michigan head coach.

photo.alt: Tommy Carr's touchdown pass in debut

stories.title: Michigan Lottery Daily 3, Daily 4 results for Sept. 19, 2026
stories.summary: The Michigan Lottery released the winning numbers for the Daily 3 and Daily 4 games on September 19, 2026. The Daily 3 midday numbers were 9-5-3, and the evening numbers were 1-1-4. For the Daily 4, the midday numbers were 9-0-3-5, and the evening numbers were 2-6-1-8.

photo.alt: Michigan Lottery Daily 3, Daily 4 results for Sept. 19, 2026

stories.title: Michigan Public names Brian Manzullo as managing editor of multiplatform news strategy
stories.summary: Michigan Public has appointed Brian Manzullo as its inaugural managing editor of multiplatform news strategy. Manzullo brings over 14 years of experience from the Detroit Free Press and The Arizona Republic to his new role, where he will strengthen the station's digital journalism and expand its reach across platforms. He will start on September 21, 2026, based in Ann Arbor.

photo.alt: Brian Manzullo headshot

stories.title: Michigan’s two major party candidates for U.S. Senate offer differing ideas for health care
stories.summary: Republican Mike Rogers proposes a health care plan focused on transparency while Democrat Abdul El-Sayed advocates for Medicare for All. The candidates' positions highlight contrasting approaches to the state's health care system.

photo.alt: Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers speaks to reporters at a campaign office in Taylor, Michigan on Saturday, September 19.

stories.title: Michigan State to face No. 3 Notre Dame in challenging road game
stories.summary: Unranked Michigan State will face No. 3 Notre Dame on the road in a 30-point underdog matchup. Coach Pat Fitzgerald's history of beating Notre Dame as both a player and coach could be crucial for the Spartans' defensive performance.

photo.alt: Al Goldis / AP

stories.title: Michigan Stock Report: Defensive Line Dominates UTEP Backfield
stories.summary: The Michigan defensive line delivered a dominant performance against UTEP, recording 3.5 of the team's four sacks and 6.5 tackles for loss. They pressured UTEP quarterback EJ Colson into negative-20 rushing yards and contributed to Jonah Lea'ea's pick-6. The unit's collective effort was a key factor in the game's outcome.

photo.alt: Michigan Wolverines running back Jordan Marshall (23) runs the ball in for a touchdown as Michigan hosts UTEP at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Sept. 19 2026.

stories.title: Michigan Supreme Court orders review of Oxford school shooter's life without parole sentence
stories.summary: The Michigan Supreme Court has directed the Court of Appeals to review Ethan Crumbley's appeal of his life without parole sentence for the 2021 Oxford High School shooting. Crumbley, 15 at the time, pleaded guilty to 24 criminal counts, including first-degree murder. The case now focuses on claims of ineffective legal representation during his trial.

photo.alt: Oakland County Prosecutor Karen McDonald proceeds with an opening statement as defendant Ethan Crumbley, right, listens, Thursday, July 27, 2023, in Pontiac, Mich. Oakland County judge Kwame Rowe is hearing evidence starting Thursday to help him decide whether the teen who killed four students and injured six others and a teacher in November 2021 at Oxford High School should be sentenced to prison without the chance of parole. (AP Photo/Carlos Osorio)

stories.title: Michigan to face UTEP in final non-conference game before Big Ten play
stories.summary: Michigan is a heavy favorite in their upcoming game against UTEP at the Big House. The Wolverines need to focus on improving their offense and preparing quarterback Bryce Underwood for tougher conference games.

photo.alt: Al Goldis / AP

stories.title: NCAA offers no relief for Western Michigan after last-second loss to Michigan
stories.summary: The NCAA confirmed that Michigan improperly received an extra second in their September 5 game against Western Michigan, which allowed them to win on a Hail Mary pass. However, the committee stated there is no mechanism to overturn the result, leaving Broncos fans without recourse.

photo.alt: Al Goldis / AP

stories.title: New House committee to examine signature verification sampling process for ballot initiatives
stories.summary: A new select committee in the Michigan House was established to review the signature verification sampling process for ballot initiatives, following a deadlock on a voter ID petition. The committee, led by Republicans, aims to ensure the process is followed correctly and address concerns about potential partisan bias in the Board of State Canvassers' decisions.

photo.alt: All four members of the Board of State Canvassers gather with Bureau of Elections staff to review signatures on the citizens-only ballot petition on Aug. 24, 2026.

stories.title: New ‘Kids Count’ data shows drop in college readiness, education participation among young adults
stories.summary: The Michigan League for Public Policy's 2026 Kids Count report shows declining college readiness and education participation among young adults, with Michigan ranking 42nd nationally in education. The report highlights increased poverty rates for children, drops in Medicaid and SNAP enrollment, and rising food insecurity, while noting an 84% increase in youth voter turnout since 2016.

photo.alt: Arabia Simeon, founder and CEO of Politics on the Go discusses youth voter turnout at a panel discussion during the Michigan League for Public Policy's Champions for Kids luncheon on Sept. 17, 2026.

stories.title: Ocelots fall to St. Clair County in straight sets
stories.summary: The Schoolcraft College women's volleyball team fell to St. Clair County Community College in straight sets (25-10, 25-18, 25-19) on Sept. 14, 2026 at Trinity Elite Sports Center. Despite improving offensively throughout the match, Schoolcraft struggled with a -.038 hitting percentage while St. Clair County controlled the game with a .253 team hitting percentage. The loss drops Schoolcraft to 4-4 overall and 0-2 in conference play, with their next game scheduled for Sept. 21 against Henry Ford.

photo.alt: Schoolcraft College volleyball action

stories.title: Pets of the week: Kutcher is struggling and needs your help. Stevie craves attention.
stories.summary: Genesee County Animal Care in Flint Township is seeking adopters for two pets. Kutcher, a struggling animal, needs help, while Stevie craves attention. Both are available for adoption at the facility located at 4351 W. Pasadena Avenue.

photo.alt: Kutcher is ready for adoption, looking for a forever home. (Photo provided by Hannah Peterson | GCAC)

stories.title: Pets of the week: Pumpkin and Mocha Mocha are looking for their forever homes
stories.summary: The Jackson County Animal Shelter features Pumpkin, a 4-year-old American Staffordshire mix, and Mocha Mocha, a 6-year-old calico cat, both available for adoption. Pumpkin enjoys walks and play, while Mocha Mocha is a calm cat who becomes affectionate once comfortable. Adoption processes include applications, meet-and-greets, and fees covering vaccinations and sterilization.

photo.alt: Pets of the week

stories.title: Police seize 2 hand grenades from deceased Hemlock resident’s home
stories.summary: Police have seized a pair of hand grenades from a Hemlock-area home. Richland Township police learned of the two potential explosive weapons at a residence in the 300 block Sandridge Drive on Thursday, Sept. 17. Officers who initially inspected the grenades believed one was decommissioned while the other appeared to be live. Officers summoned a member from the Michigan State Police Bomb Squad to the scene. The trooper confirmed both grenades were live and operable.

photo.alt: Police seize 2 hand grenades from deceased Hemlock resident’s home

stories.title: Proposed repeal of ‘Roadless Rule’ could open Michigan national forests to logging, roadbuilding
stories.summary: The U.S. Forest Service proposes to rescind the 2001 Roadless Rule, which would allow logging and road construction in Michigan's national forests. Environmental advocates argue this could increase wildfire risks and harm critical habitats, with public comments due by Sept. 21.

photo.alt: Overlook from the Trap Hills within the Ottawa National Forest, Western U.P.

stories.title: Rural women who got C-sections more likely to be prescribed opioids at home, study finds
stories.summary: Women giving birth in rural communities were more likely than urban peers to receive opioid prescriptions after a C-section, according to a study of 540,000 cases. The analysis found 10 more rural women per 100 C-sections received opioids post-discharge compared to urban areas, with rural patients also more likely to get acetaminophen and NSAIDs.

photo.alt: Births in Florida

stories.title: Saginaw man, 71, charged with drunkenly crashing into stopped Michigan State Police vehicle
stories.summary: A Saginaw man has been charged with a felony two months after allegedly drunkenly crashing into a Michigan State Police patrol vehicle. Prosecutors on Sept. 8 issued a warrant for the 71-year-old man, charging him with third-offense operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated and driving with an open alcohol container. The first charge is a five-year felony, while the second is a 90-day misdemeanor.

photo.alt: Saginaw man, 71, charged with drunkenly crashing into stopped Michigan State Police vehicle

stories.title: Saginaw man gets prison time for stabbing, trying to kill man at East Side gas station
stories.summary: A Saginaw man is prison-bound for repeatedly stabbing and trying to kill a man at an East Side gas station in an apparent dispute over childcare. Saginaw County Circuit Judge Darnell Jackson on Thursday, Sept. 17, sentenced 52-year-old Donald A. Williams to five to 15 years in prison. He gave Williams credit for 301 days already served in the county jail and ordered him to pay $198 in fines and costs.

photo.alt: Saginaw man gets prison time for stabbing, trying to kill man at East Side gas station

stories.title: Sept. 19 Powerball results: 31 players come heartbreakingly close to winning the $298M jackpot
stories.summary: More than two dozen players were one ball away from winning the grand prize, but there was no winner of the $298 million Powerball jackpot for the drawing held on Saturday, Sept. 19.

stories.title: Sept. 19 Powerball results: 31 players come heartbreakingly close to winning the $298M jackpot
stories.summary: No winner claimed the $298 million Powerball jackpot in the Sept. 19 drawing, with 31 players coming one ball short. A New York player won $1 million by matching all five white balls, while 30 others won $50,000 by matching four white balls and the Powerball. The next drawing on Sept. 21 will have a $313 million jackpot.

photo.alt: Powerball results for Sept. 19

stories.title: She was supposed to care for her vulnerable uncle. Feds say Detroit woman misused his money instead
stories.summary: A Detroit woman is facing federal charges after allegedly stealing thousands from her uncle with dementia. Laura Whisenant is accused of spending over $120,000 on personal expenses while leaving her uncle in deplorable living conditions without running water, electricity, or heat. The Social Security Administration suspended payments after she failed to provide documentation for the funds' use.

photo.alt: Laura Whisenant facing federal charges

stories.title: Six hospitalized after toxic chemical released from fighter jet crash in Northern Michigan
stories.summary: Six of 33 people treated for contamination were hospitalized at Munson Medical Center after a fighter jet crash released a toxic chemical in Northern Michigan. The incident occurred when the military plane crashed in Grand Traverse County.

photo.alt: The Munson Medical Center in Traverse City.

stories.summary: Skyline’s DECA club is set to have their first kickoff meeting on Monday, September 21, 2026, at 3:00 PM. The meeting will be held in Room C205, or the business magnet (BMIT) room. An international...

stories.title: Soldier’s Angels
stories.summary: Soldiers’ Angels is a national non-profit organization providing aid to veterans, deployed military, and their families through services like food distributions, transportation, and care packages. The organization offers both virtual and in-person volunteering opportunities for those interested in supporting their mission.

photo.alt: Soldiers’ Angels volunteers distributing care packages

stories.title: Stateside: Friday, Sept. 18, 2026
stories.summary: The Stateside podcast explores federal power plant emission rollbacks' climate impact, features Traverse City chefs for a long weekend, and discusses writer Lillian Li's novel 'Bad Asians' about high-achievers during the Great Recession.

photo.alt: Stateside with April Baer podcast artwork

stories.title: Steward of Democracy
stories.summary: Michael Siegrist, a former Schoolcraft alumnus and township clerk, emphasizes the integrity of the election system and was awarded Michigan Association of Municipal Clerks Township Clerk of the Year. He advocates for maintaining election sanctity and encourages involvement in the democratic process through certification programs.

photo.alt: Michael Siegrist

stories.title: Supporters of Broadway Bridge bike lanes say opponents are jumping the gun
stories.summary: City officials say opponents of proposed bike lanes on the Broadway Bridge on Ann Arbor’s northside are jumping the gun. They also say an extension of the bike lanes on Division Street is long overdue. The Division Street Bikeway Extension Project is in two phases, with the first running from Catherine Street to the bridge. Council member Lisa Disch emphasizes the need for safer infrastructure to adapt to new residents and public amenities.

photo.alt: The Broadway Bridge near Northside Grill in Ann Arbor.

stories.title: SVSU opens free outdoor fitness court with Priority Health
stories.summary: Saginaw Valley State University will officially open a new outdoor fitness facility, offering free exercise access to students and the surrounding community. The SVSU Priority Health Fitness Court will debut Wednesday, Sept. 23 at 4:30 p.m. near the main entrance of the university, west of Bachand Hall. stories.title: Unless a buyer steps up, the Toledo Blade to print last edition at the end of the year
stories.summary: The Toledo Blade, a nearly 200-year-old newspaper in Northwest Ohio, will print its final edition by year's end unless a buyer emerges. Current owners Block Communications made the decision due to unsustainable financial losses, following a rejected contract proposal by the NewsGuild that would have cut benefits and allowed AI to replace journalists. The paper previously avoided closure when a nonprofit bought The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette under similar circumstances.

source.name: Beenish Ahmed, The Associated Press, Stateside Staff

stories.title: Why does the U.P. have a volcanic ridge?
stories.summary: Michigan's Upper Peninsula, particularly the Keweenaw Peninsula, was shaped by massive volcanic activity over a billion years ago. The Greenstone Flow, part of the Midcontinent Rift System, created the region's ridge and valley topography and contributed to the formation of Lake Superior. This geological history also led to copper deposits that influenced the area's industrial and cultural development.

photo.alt: Greenstone Flow last gasps

stories.title: Why this Detroit tenants lawsuit is making landlords nervous
stories.summary: A Detroit tenants union is suing the 36th District Court, arguing that landlords should not be allowed to evict tenants or collect rent for properties without a certificate of compliance. Landlords warn this could destabilize Detroit's rental market, potentially leading to foreclosures and higher rents, while tenants hope it will force improvements in housing conditions.
